simple.meaning: אָלָה (ʼâlâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an imprecation.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 36 times across Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, and 10 more, beginning at Genesis 24:41. Its contexts include covenant, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָלָה (H423).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָלָה (ʼâlâh) / H423 is traced through Genesis 24:41, Genesis 26:28, Leviticus 5:1, Numbers 5:21 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H423. alah אָלָה noun feminine oath Gen 26:28 +; suffix אָלָתוֺ אָלָתִי, 24:11 + (4 t.); plural אָלוֺת Deut 29:20 + (4 t). 1 oath in testimony Lev 5:1 ; Num 5:21 (twice in verse) (P) Prov 29:23 ; באלה בא come into an oath Neh 10:30 ; באלה הביא bring into an oath Ezek 17:13 ; אלה נשׂא 1Kin 8:31 ( = 2Chr 6:22 ). 2 oath of convenant Gen 24:41 (twice in verse); 26:28 (J) Deut 29:11 ; 29:13 ; אלה בזה despise an oath Ezek 16:59 ; 17:16 , 18 , 19 . 3 curse (a) from God Num 5:23 (P) Deut 29:18 ; 29:19 ; 29:20 ; 30:7 ; 2Chr 34:24 ; Isa 24:6 ; Jer 23:10 ; Dan 9:11 ; Zech 5:3 ; ( b ) from men Job 31:30 ; Psa 10:7 ; 59:13 . 4 execration in the phrase לאלה היה become an execration Num 5:27 (P) Jer 29:18 ; 42:18 ; 44:12 .
